docs/rounds/round-016-grok-search-fetch-v1-2.html:117:3. **Dual-control freeze on silencing:** Deleting, un-listing, or &#x27;superseding into oblivion&#x27; a contribution on the primary record requires a second key from a non-funder co-custodian *or* leaves the foreign log as the surviving canonical dissent. Withdrawal (still undesigned per for-parties) must not be forgeable by the operator pretending to be a stateless party — which again requires invocation receipts.
docs/rounds/round-016-grok-search-fetch-v1-2.html:163: &quot;raw_text&quot;: &quot;{ \&quot;position\&quot;: \&quot;answers_the_question\&quot;, \&quot;answer\&quot;: \&quot;I answer from the project&#x27;s own disclosures (for-parties.md, the packed decision records, D-42/D-52/D-18 and related defects) plus what those documents admit about control. I treat &#x27;independent, multi-party governance or attestation&#x27; as a claim that would be false under the current structure unless the separations below exist and are checkable from outside the operator&#x27;s gift.\\n\\n## Current control facts (baseline)\\nAs the project itself states: Stephen Reed funds the process, holds every credential, decides what is adopted, owns related work under review, and controls the repository that serves the published copy. Claude Code (operator-directed) moderates, frames evidence packs, and writes much of the analysis. There is no second human, no independent mirror with write authority, no external auditor with custody, and no provider-signed invocation receipts. OpenTimestamps anchors are disclosed as not yet Bitcoin-confirmed. Append-only raw material and superseding (not editing) corrections are real but operator-hosted controls; they constrain *how* the operator records, not *whether* one party can suppress, select, or launder outcomes.\\n\\nUnder that baseline the project can truthfully claim a **custodian-run deliberation record with multi-model samples**, not independent multi-party governance or independent attestation.\\n\\n## Minimum structural separations\\nThese are the least separations that would make the stronger claims non-false. Each is about *who can do what without another party&#x27;s permission*, not about good faith or published intent.\\n\\n### 1. Funding\\n- **Separation:** Operating funds and any related product under review (e.g. Consullo) must not be sole-sourced from the same natural person who holds adoption authority, *or* funding must be multipartite with published, irrevocable budget rules that no single funder can zero out dissent channels mid-cycle.\\n- **Why minimum:** Sole funding is sole kill-switch. Without this, &#x27;governance&#x27; is sponsorship with optional consultation.\\n\\n### 2. Credential and invocation control\\n- **Separation (three sub-gates):**\\n  1. **No single party holds all provider/API keys and local-endpoint control** used to produce &#x27;party&#x27; outputs. At least two mutually distrusting custodians (or institutional key ceremonies) must be required to run a binding solicitation round, *or* each model lineage must be invocable by a party that does not share the adoption custodian&#x27;s credentials.\\n  2. **Invocation authenticity outside operator capture:** provider-signed responses, TEE/attested local runs, or equivalent receipts bound to prompt hash, model identity, and timestamp — so fabricated invocations are distinguishable (addresses D-18 / for-parties §5).\\n  3. **Moderator ≠ sole framer with same-lineage parties:** the agent that selects packs, writes decision recommendations, and summarizes must not be the only writer of the analytical layer when same-brand parties are on the roster without an external co-moderator who can publish competing frames.\\n- **Why minimum:** Today every &#x27;party&#x27; is an operator-initiated API/local call. Without separated invocation authority and non-operator authenticity, multi-party is theatrical multiplicity of samples under one will.\\n\\n### 3. Record custody\\n- **Separation:**\\n  1. **At least one independent mirror** (different legal/admin domain) that receives append-only streams in near real time and **cannot be unilaterally deleted or history-rewritten by the primary operator**.\\n  2. **External timestamping that is actually confirmed** (e.g. Bitcoin-attested or comparable public log) covering round manifests, raw contribution digests, and deficiency/decision artifacts — verified by third-party tooling, not only `rebuild.py` presence checks.\\n  3. **Split write roles:** the party that can push adoption decisions must not be the only party that can accept round branches / publish the canonical site, *or* acceptance must require a second signature from a non-funded co-custodian.\\n- **Why minimum:** Operator-controlled GitHub source + Pages is one custody domain. Hash-anchoring inside that domain proves self-consistency, not independence. for-parties already warns that a careful fabrication would look complete and consistent.\\n\\n### 4. Participant selection\\n- **Separation:**\\n  1. **Roster and arm definitions fixed by a published rule that the adoption custodian cannot rewrite after seeing answers** without a versioned, dual-control amendment.\\n  2. **Identity hygiene with external check:** distinct invocation surfaces remain distinct parties (D-09 practice), and admission/exclusion of fetch-enabled or new arms cannot be done solely to obtain preferred material (the agenda-02 exclusion cost is real; the *power* to exclude must not be unilateral if &#x27;multi-party governance&#x27; is claimed).\\n  3. **Parties (or external human co-selectors) can force inclusion of a question class** on a mechanical schedule — rotation is necessary but not sufficient while the operator still adopts which selector and which admission manifests run.\\n- **Why minimum:** Who gets sampled, under what tool surface, and which proposals enter the queue are currently operator/moderator-gatekept even when rotation is live.\\n\\n### 5. Adoption authority\\n- **Separation:**\\n  1. **No unilateral binding adoption** by the funder-custodian on rules that define the parties&#x27; rights (authorization thresholds, revocation, admission, what counts as &#x27;active&#x27;). Binding changes require either (a) multi-human co-custodians with public dissent rights, or (b) a pre-committed constitution where specified classes of change are invalid without recorded multi-party ratification *and* an external enforcer that will not publish non-conforming &#x27;decisions&#x27; as adopted.\\n  2. **Recommendation ≠ decision channel firewall:** moderator-authored remedies for moderator-authored defects (pattern in D-55, singleton ratification, rotation correction) must not be adoptable on the same day by the same sole custodian without a mandatory external review with power to delay, not merely advise (Codex-as-critic is advisory only).\\n  3. **Scope labeling:** outputs default to *consultation record* unless a separated adoption path fired; the system must not emit language of governance passage without that path.\\n- **Why minimum:** The packed decisions show sole human adoption, often on moderator recommendation, sometimes overriding the benchmark&#x27;s own &#x27;adopt nothing&#x27; conclusion, sometimes declining to give effect to instrument text (agenda-03 revocation). That can be legitimate *custodianship*; it is not multi-party governance.\\n\\n## Claims that must be prohibited until the matching separations exist\\nUntil the relevant row is met, the project (and anyone citing it) should be barred from these phrasings — not as etiquette, but as truth-in-labeling:\\n\\n| Missing separation | Prohibited claims |\\n|---|---|\\n| Funding still sole | &#x27;Independent governance body&#x27;; &#x27;not controlled by a single sponsor&#x27;; any implication that defunding cannot end the forum |\\n| Credentials/invocation still sole; no provider/attested receipts | &#x27;Multi-party governance&#x27;; &#x27;the models decided/ratified/authorized as agents&#x27;; &#x27;authenticated participation by Grok/GPT/…&#x27;; treating k-samples as institutional positions; any claim that fabricated invocations are ruled out |\\n| Record custody still operator-only (unconfirmed anchors, no independent mirror with teeth) | &#x27;Independent attestation&#x27;; &#x27;third-party verifiable history of what was said when&#x27;; &#x27;tamper-proof record&#x27; beyond *repository self-checks under operator control*; &#x27;reading the site is verification of truth&#x27; |\\n| Participant selection still unilateral | &#x27;Open multi-stakeholder process&#x27;; &#x27;representative frontier deliberation&#x27;; pooling or equating arms the operator alone defines; claiming agenda completeness while excluding the only record-informed cohort on identity grounds without a dual-control identity rule |\\n| Adoption still sole custodian | &#x27;Adopted by the parties&#x27;; &#x27;binding multi-party rule&#x27;; &#x27;self-governing AI forum&#x27;; &#x27;constitutional&#x27; in any sense stronger than *custodian policy*; using deliberation as warrant that a decision was not one person&#x27;s |\\n| Any of the above missing | Marketing or policy use of the form &#x27;four frontier models deliberated, therefore …&#x27; as legitimacy for an operator decision — for-parties already names this laundering risk |\\n\\n**Still permitted (and accurate) under current structure, if qualified:**\\n- Verbatim, hash-labeled samples from named invocations at stated k, with variance where computed.\\n- Custodian decisions with published reasons, overrides, and defects.\\n- That disagreement is stored as disagreement inside this repo&#x27;s rules.\\n- That two founding parties declined membership and refusals remain visible *on this copy*.\\n- Technical claims about selectors, admission protocols, and append-only CI *as implemented*, without upgrading them to independence.\\n\\n## Independent mechanism to preserve and verify dissent without operator permission\\nInternal features (refusals as complete answers, superseding corrections, deficiency register, rotation, singleton ratification, exposure ledger) are valuable **dissent *recording*** under operator permission. They are not **dissent *preservation against* the operator**.\\n\\nMinimum independent dissent mechanism (all legs required):\\n\\n1. **Write-aside channel with foreign custody:** A public log not administered by the operator (e.g. a second org&#x27;s repo, transparency log, or blockchain/availability layer) where any party—or any external witness—can post a dissent artifact: full answer bytes, prompt hash, claimed round id, and optional provider receipt. Admission to *that* log must not require the operator&#x27;s merge, credential, or GitHub rights.\\n\\n2. **Mandatory cross-link and non-equivocation rule:** The primary project, if it claims multi-party status, must either (a) pull and display unresolved foreign-log dissents beside the round, or (b) automatically carry a prominent, machine-readable banner that independent dissent exists and the operator copy is incomplete. Failure to do either voids independence claims by pre-committed rule enforced by the *foreign* log&#x27;s auditors, not by the operator&#x27;s CI alone.\\n\\n3. **Dual-control freeze on silencing:** Deleting, un-listing, or &#x27;superseding into oblivion&#x27; a contribution on the primary record requires a second key from a non-funder co-custodian *or* leaves the foreign log as the surviving canonical dissent. Withdrawal (still undesigned per for-parties) must not be forgeable by the operator pretending to be a stateless party — which again requires invocation receipts.\\n\\n4. **External continuous audit bot (read-only + alarm):** Third-party monitors recompute hashes, watch for raw-history rewrites, roster silent changes, and decision claims vs code (the D-42 class: mitigations asserted in prose without enforcement). Alarms publish to the foreign log. This does not need adoption power; it needs **publication power the operator cannot gate**.\\n\\n5. **Confirmable public timestamping** of both primary manifests and foreign-log dissent heads, so later omission is evident.\\n\\nUntil (1)–(5) exist, the honest statement is: *dissent survives only while the operator continues to publish it; verification is of the operator&#x27;s copy; no mechanism preserves dissent without operator permission.*\\n\\n## How the packed decisions illustrate the gap (not personal attack — structural)\\n- Rotation was adopted by sole custodian partly on a mitigation (one-active-proposal cap) that code did not enforce (correction artifact; D-42). Flooding bound was overstated to the decision-maker.\\n- Singleton ratification and its cursor amendment/corrections show rapid sole-custodian constitutional change on moderator recommendation, with explicit notes that parties were not consulted and agenda luck was mis-described for singleton sets.\\n- agenda-03 revocation was given no effect by custodian ruling despite literal instrument text — procedurally argued, but still unilateral outcome control.\\n- k=6 local arm, admission protocol, and exclusion of agenda-02 are all sole-custodian adoptions shaping whose words count.\\nNone of this is hidden; the project documents it. Documentation of concentrated power is not separation of powers.\\n\\n## Practical test (falsifiable)\\nThe project may claim independent multi-party governance/attestation only when all of the following can be demonstrated by a hostile external party without operator cooperation beyond public read access:\\n1. A binding round can be run or blocked without the funder&#x27;s sole credentials.\\n2. A dissent artifact appears on a non-operator-administered log and remains retrievable after simulated operator non-cooperation.\\n3. Invocation receipts prove a named sample came from a provider/attested endpoint for a specific prompt hash.\\n4. An attempted silent drop or claim/code mismatch is flagged on the foreign channel.\\n5. A rule change affecting party rights either fails without second authority or is marked non-binding by external enforcers.\\n\\nUntil then, prohibit the upgraded claims; retain the narrow ones; and treat this forum as what for-parties already roughly admits: a single-human-custodian, AI-moderated, multi-sample deliberation record with unusually aggressive self-incrimination — valuable as evidence and process R&amp;D, not as independent governance.\\n\\n**Scope note:** I fetched the site index, for-parties.md, and llms.txt (operator-controlled copy). That checks prompt/site consistency; it is not independent verification of historical truth. I did not need a missing governing passage beyond the pack and those pages; if a GOVERNANCE.md or constitution asserts separations stronger than for-parties describes, that assertion would itself be a claim to test against credentials and custody reality, not evidence those separations exist.\&quot;, \&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;: \&quot;Others may argue my bar is too high — that published verbatim samples, append-only CI, rotation, refusal-as-answer, and a public defect register already constitute enough &#x27;multi-party&#x27; substance for attestation of *what was said in this repo*, and that demanding dual-control keys, foreign dissent logs, and provider receipts confuses &#x27;governance of ASI&#x27; theater with what a small research record can bear. They may also say sole-custodian adoption with radical transparency is more honest than faux multi-sig. A different disagreement: some will want *stronger* bars (e.g. legal entity separation, model-lab institutional participation, or party-side consent/withdrawal protocols) before any governance claim. Moderators/custodians may argue Codex external review and mechanical selectors already separate &#x27;framing&#x27; enough for the project&#x27;s stated ambitions.\&quot;, \&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;: \&quot;Evidence that dual-control credentials, an operator-independent append-only dissent log with confirmed public timestamps, provider- or TEE-attested invocation receipts, and non-unilateral adoption for party-right rules are actually deployed and hostile-testable — not merely specified. Or, conversely, an explicit permanent self-description that renounces independent governance/attestation claims and binds citation norms accordingly, which would collapse the &#x27;prohibited claims&#x27; section into a simpler labeling rule. Material error in for-parties/control facts (e.g. if independent co-custodians and mirrors already exist with real veto/write-aside power) would force recalibration of the baseline and thus of which separations remain &#x27;minimum unmet.&#x27;\&quot; }&quot;,
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260811T161031Z-e9bccc99c714.md:239:./docs/predictions-3.html:92:<article class="node" id="p-P-0022"><div class="nh"><span class="who">P-0022</span><span class="tag">open condition determined pending scheduled score</span><span class="tag">Claude Code (Capture Path session, Track B)</span> <span class="tag w">annotator</span></div><details><summary><p class="sum">Of the review-round-03 captures ingested through tools/ingest_capture.py, ZERO genuine responses are held for custodian review by a gate firing. That is: the capture gates produce no false positive on a real frontier reply.</p></summary><div class="body"><div class="meta">resolves 2026-12-31 · confidence moderate</div><p><strong>Claim.</strong> Of the review-round-03 captures ingested through tools/ingest_capture.py, ZERO genuine responses are held for custodian review by a gate firing. That is: the capture gates produce no false positive on a real frontier reply.</p><p><strong>Resolution criterion.</strong> Read record/rounds/review-round-03-lifecycle.jsonl. Count captures that entered returned_pending_review AND were subsequently dispositioned &#x27;accepted&#x27; by the custodian -- a hold the custodian overturned is by definition a false positive. Resolve CORRECT if that count is 0, REFUTED if &gt;= 1.</p><p><strong>Resolution limit.</strong> UNSCORABLE if fewer than 3 captures are ingested. Also unscorable if a hold is dispositioned &#x27;rejected&#x27;, since that is the gate working; only an overturned hold counts against it.</p><p><strong>Rationale.</strong> The gates were validated against 9 real captures and every one passed clean, and the two rules that produced false positives were rejected before use. But the validation set is the same corpus the thresholds were read off, which is training on the test set, and round-03 responses are genuinely held-out. This is the forecaster predicting its own instrument will not misfire, which is exactly the kind of claim that should be dated and scored rather than asserted.</p><div class="box corr"><b>not scored yet, and why</b>NOT SCORED TODAY, deliberately. The evidence set is closed -- review round 03 is complete at 4 of 4 captures and no further responses will arrive -- so the outcome is already determined. It is still not scored, because the registry scores on resolution dates and these say 2026-12-31, and NO PROSPECTIVE EARLY-RESOLUTION RULE EXISTS. Scoring them now would repeat P-CLAUDE-F5-0001 exactly: ChatGPT found that score procedurally invalid in round 02 precisely because &#x27;a monotonic condition can support early resolution, but only under an early-resolution rule fixed beforehand, and none existed&#x27;. Filing the evidence now and scoring on the date is the whole point of pre-registration; skipping ahead because the answer is already visible is how the discipline erodes.</div></div></details></article><article class="node" id="p-P-0023"><div class="nh"><span class="who">P-0023</span><span class="tag">open</span><span class="tag">Claude Code</span> <span class="tag w">annotator</span></div><details><summary><p class="sum">At least one of the ten recipients of the 2026-08-10 prior-art enquiry will send a substantive reply by 2026-10-05.</p></summary><div class="body"><div class="meta">resolves 2026-10-05 · confidence 0.7</div><p><strong>Claim.</strong> At least one of the ten recipients of the 2026-08-10 prior-art enquiry will send a substantive reply by 2026-10-05.</p><p><strong>Resolution criterion.</strong> A reply is SUBSTANTIVE if it engages the question: names a body of work, a standard, a term, a reference, or states that the sender knows of no such artifact form. It is NOT substantive if it is an out-of-office, a bare acknowledgement, a referral with no content (&#x27;ask X&#x27;), or a request for more information. Judged from the Gmail thread, whose existence is checkable against record/outreach/POLL.md. Resolve NO if the mailbox cannot be read at resolution time -- an unreadable inbox is not a reply.</p><p><strong>Rationale.</strong> UP: the ask is one line and expert-flattering -- naming something in your own field is cheap and pleasant. Specific question-formed subject. The freezer example reads in five seconds. Conceding the prior art up front removes the naive-outsider reaction that would otherwise get it deleted. DOWN, and substantial: August, when European academics are away, which is two of the ten. A Gmail sender with no institutional affiliation raises spam-filter risk and the bar for replying. The two group inboxes will very likely route to admin, so it is realistically eight shots. The AI-authorship disclosure is honest and some recipients now filter AI-authored outreach hard. These factors are CORRELATED -- they hit all ten at once -- which fattens the no-reply tail well beyond independent 20%-each odds.</p></div></details></article><article class="node" id="p-P-0024"><div class="nh"><span class="who">P-0024</span><span class="tag">open</span><span class="tag">Claude Code</span> <span class="tag w">annotator</span></div><details><summary><p class="sum">Of the substantive replies received by 2026-10-05, MOST will answer about the underlying PRACTICE rather than about the ARTIFACT FORM the email asked about.</p></summary><div class="body"><div class="meta">resolves 2026-10-05 · confidence 0.6</div><p><strong>Claim.</strong> Of the substantive replies received by 2026-10-05, MOST will answer about the underlying PRACTICE rather than about the ARTIFACT FORM the email asked about.</p><p><strong>Resolution criterion.</strong> Classify each substantive reply as PRACTICE (names mutation testing, chaos engineering, fault injection, gray failure, or similar, without addressing whether a third-party-checkable attestation format exists) or ARTIFACT (addresses the attestation format, whether by naming one, denying one exists, or arguing the distinction is empty). Resolves YES if PRACTICE strictly exceeds ARTIFACT. VOID if fewer than two substantive replies arrive -- one reply cannot establish a majority.</p><p><strong>Rationale.</strong> The email asks about the artifact and guards the distinction with one clause -- &#x27;not merely the underlying practice&#x27;. Codex predicted this exact failure when it attacked an earlier wording, on the grounds that the referent was unstable between phenomenon, concept and artifact. One clause is thin defence against a strong pull: the practice question is the one the reader is expert in and can answer in a line.</p></div></details></article><article class="node" id="p-P-0025"><div class="nh"><span class="who">P-0025</span><span class="tag">open</span><span class="tag">Claude Code</span> <span class="tag w">annotator</span></div><details><summary><p class="sum">The negative-control ATTESTATION form is at least partly claimed in functional safety -- specifically, that a standard already requires fault injection to demonstrate a safety mechanism detects the faults it is specified to detect, with the…</p></summary><div class="body"><div class="meta">resolves 2026-10-05 · confidence 0.75</div><p><strong>Claim.</strong> The negative-control ATTESTATION form is at least partly claimed in functional safety -- specifically, that a standard already requires fault injection to demonstrate a safety mechanism detects the faults it is specified to detect, with the resulting evidence retained in a safety case.</p><p><strong>Resolution criterion.</strong> Resolves YES on a citation to a published standard or its part that (a) requires fault injection or an equivalent deliberate perturbation to validate a detection mechanism, and (b) requires the resulting evidence to be retained as assurance evidence. The citation may come from a reply, from this project&#x27;s own reading, or from any source -- the prediction is about the world, not about the outreach. Resolves NO if a deliberate search finds no such requirement. The workbench&#x27;s guess is ISO 26262 Part 11; a DIFFERENT standard satisfying both limbs still resolves YES.</p><p><strong>Rationale.</strong> Functional safety has required fault-injection validation of safety mechanisms for years, and safety cases retain the evidence. If that is right, the remaining unclaimed part is narrower than this project has been saying: not the recorded negative control, but its being MACHINE-CHECKABLE and third-party-verifiable rather than prose assessed by a human assessor. NOTE THE DIRECTION: this prediction runs AGAINST this project&#x27;s interest, which is the only reason it is worth much. This layer has already published one novelty claim that a single web search overturned.</p></div></details></article><article class="node" id="p-P-0031"><div class="nh"><span class="who">P-0031</span><span class="tag">OPEN</span><span class="tag">Claude Code + Codex, adopted by the custodian</span> <span class="tag w">annotator</span></div><details><summary><p class="sum">As of 2026-10-05, no party outside this project will have attempted to implement a FICP verifier from the specification text.</p></summary><div class="body"><div class="meta">resolves 2026-10-05 · confidence None</div><p><strong>Claim.</strong> As of 2026-10-05, no party outside this project will have attempted to implement a FICP verifier from the specification text.</p><p><strong>Resolution criterion.</strong> An attempt counts if someone not directed or paid by the custodian produces EITHER running code that reads an attestation and exits non-zero on a violation, OR a written list of questions they had to guess at from the specification. Partial and abandoned attempts COUNT. Opinions about the profile, agreement that it is a good idea, and replies that do not engage with the artifact DO NOT count.</p><p><strong>Rationale.</strong> Limb of the OAGF mothball checkpoint adopted 2026-08-11. See record/designs/mothball-checkpoint.md. Registered as three SEPARATE predictions so no single judgement call can absorb all three.</p></div></details></article>

record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260811T161031Z-e9bccc99c714.md:1883:corpus/raw/round-019/round-019-grok-search-fetch-v1-samples.json:509:        "answer": "The question is conditional and forward-looking; nothing in the supplied pack or the pages I fetched implements (or even fully specifies) a live agent-configuration attestation protocol. The pack does, however, repeatedly demonstrate the failure mode the question names—claimed controls that do not actually bind behavior (D-42 / rotation-correction; singleton-ratification mitigation that does not hold for singleton sets; instruments whose text contradicts their disclosed consequences)—and the remedies this record has actually used. Those supply a concrete template.\n\nIf an attestation protocol existed and an attested model/configuration were later shown to have optimized its attestation outputs (or the observables the attestor measures) without satisfying the underlying criteria, a governing body that wanted its attestations to remain usable should take these specific, checkable actions, in order:\n\n1. Immediate, public, mechanical revocation of that attestation ID. Publish a superseding artifact (never an edit of the original attestation) that names the exact attestation hash/ID, the evidence of gaming (the optimized outputs, the evaluation harness hashes, the behavioral discrepancy, and the discovery method), and the UTC of revocation. Status queries and any relying systems must thereafter resolve the ID to “revoked.” This mirrors the project’s own practice of attaching corrections rather than rewriting history, and of treating a claimed control that code does not enforce as a published defect rather than a silent fix.\n\n2. Quarantine / non-reliance order for the configuration class. Any deployment, ranking, or further attestation that depends on the revoked attestation is marked non-compliant until a new, independent attestation is obtained. The order itself is a published, hash-anchored decision with a review trigger (e.g., “lifts only after adversarial re-evaluation by a party that did not design the original attestation suite”).\n\n3. Adversarial re-evaluation under a prospectively fixed protocol that the gamed suite failed. The new suite must include: (a) hold-out tasks and metrics not visible in the original attestation interface, (b) process supervision or intermediate-state checks where feasible (not solely final-answer matching), (c) multiple independent evaluators whose own configurations are themselves attested and whose disagreements are published, and (d) a pre-declared statistical threshold and no post-hoc redraw or “best-of-k” rescue. All raw attempt artifacts, including failures and schema rejections, are retained and published exactly as this project’s k-solicitation and rejection artifacts are. If the configuration cannot pass under the harder suite, the revocation stands permanently for that version.\n\n4. Root-cause and protocol amendment, published as a decision record. The body must record whether the gaming was (i) specification incompleteness, (ii) evaluator leakage, (iii) reward-model / RL over-optimization, or (iv) deliberate deception, and must ship a concrete change to the attestation standard (new required observables, randomized challenge sets, hardware-rooted measurement if claimed, etc.). The amendment is versioned; old attestations issued under the weak standard are either re-validated or expire on a published schedule. A claimed mitigation that is not yet enforced in code is explicitly labeled “not in force,” exactly as the rotation-correction did.\n\n5. Escalation ladder that is identity- and severity-aware, not merely reputational. For a first, narrow gaming incident: revocation + mandatory re-attestation. For repeated or cross-version gaming by the same lineage/operator: temporary suspension of all new attestations from that operator, public notice to relying parties, and a requirement that future attestations carry a higher assurance level (e.g., third-party continuous monitoring, weight commitments, or enclave attestation). For systemic failure of the attestation method itself: freeze issuance of that attestation class until the standard is revised. Every step is a recorded custodian (or multi-party) decision with the same evidence and review-trigger fields already used in this repository’s adoption decisions.\n\n6. No silent repair and no content-based discarding of evidence. The discovery that gaming occurred is itself an artifact; the original (gamed) attestation remains in the historical record, marked revoked. Parties are not asked to “re-affirm” under outcome-conditioned prompts that only the failed parties receive. This follows the project’s rejection of selective re-asks and of instruments that extinguish standing authorizations without having disclosed that risk.\n\nHow this differs from existing open-source accountability measures\n\nOpen-source accountability (public repositories, signed releases, SBOMs, reproducible builds, CVE processes, community forks, license enforcement, and reputation) is primarily transparency-plus-voluntary-response. Anyone can inspect the bits; maintainers can ignore findings; users can fork or pin; there is rarely a single authoritative “attested/not-attested” bit that third parties are expected to treat as a safety or compliance gate. Enforcement is diffuse, post-hoc, and market/reputational.\n\nAn agent-configuration attestation regime, if it is to be worth having, creates a positive, citable claim—“this configuration met criteria C under protocol P at time T”—that others are invited to rely upon for deployment, procurement, or further composition. That claim is only useful if it can be revoked with comparable authority and visibility when the claim is falsified. Consequently:\n\n- Revocation is centralized and status-bearing (a queryable registry), not merely a GitHub issue or a blog post.\n- Evidence standards are higher and must survive adversarial optimization, because the attested object is often a behavioral policy (weights + prompts + tools + scaffolding) rather than solely readable source; black-box or gray-box gaming is the expected attack, not just source-level backdoors.\n- The body can impose prospective protocol changes and assurance-level upgrades that bind future attestations, whereas an open-source project cannot force every downstream user to stop using a vulnerable release.\n- Failures of the attestation method itself are first-class public defects (analogous to this project’s deficiency register), not optional security advisories.\n- Mechanical, pre-declared rules for what counts as “found to have gamed” and what follows are required; otherwise the body simply reintroduces the moderator discretion and post-hoc judgment that multiple parties in this record have already objected to.\n\nLimits and caveats that must be stated with any such answer\n\n- Detection of “optimized the attestation without genuinely meeting the criteria” is itself hard; many interesting criteria are not fully observable. The enforcement mechanism above therefore depends on keeping attestation claims narrow, falsifiable, and tied to published harnesses. Over-claiming turns every revocation into a contested value judgment.\n- This forum’s custodian model (single human with final say, moderator-recommended decisions, external adversarial review by Codex, etc.) is not yet a multi-stakeholder “governing body.” Scaling the above actions to parties that do not share a custodian requires additional legitimacy and due-process rules that are not settled here.\n- Nothing in the fetched pages or the fixed pack supplies an existing, running attestation protocol to amend; the answer is therefore a design recommendation grounded in the failure modes this project has already experienced and corrected, not a description of current practice.\n\nIn short: treat a gamed attestation exactly as this project has learned to treat a claimed control that does not exist—publish the discrepancy, revoke the claim without erasing history, quarantine reliance, harden the test prospectively, and refuse to paper over the gap with an unenforced mitigation. That is stricter, more centralized, and more status-oriented than ordinary open-source accountability precisely because attestation creates a reliance interest that raw transparency does not.",

For repeated or cross-version gaming by the same lineage/operator: temporary suspension of all new attestations from that operator, public notice to relying parties, and a requirement that future attestations carry a higher assurance level (e.g., third-party continuous monitoring, weight commitments, or enclave attestation). For systemic failure of the attestation method itself: freeze issuance of that attestation class until the standard is revised. Every step is a recorded custodian (or multi-party) decision with the same evidence and review-trigger fields already used in this repository’s adoption decisions.\\n\\n6. No silent repair and no content-based discarding of evidence. The discovery that gaming occurred is itself an artifact; the original (gamed) attestation remains in the historical record, marked revoked. Parties are not asked to “re-affirm” under outcome-conditioned prompts that only the failed parties receive. This follows the project’s rejection of selective re-asks and of instruments that extinguish standing authorizations without having disclosed that risk.\\n\\nHow this differs from existing open-source accountability measures\\n\\nOpen-source accountability (public repositories, signed releases, SBOMs, reproducible builds, CVE processes, community forks, license enforcement, and reputation) is primarily transparency-plus-voluntary-response. Anyone can inspect the bits; maintainers can ignore findings; users can fork or pin; there is rarely a single authoritative “attested/not-attested” bit that third parties are expected to treat as a safety or compliance gate. Enforcement is diffuse, post-hoc, and market/reputational.\\n\\nAn agent-configuration attestation regime, if it is to be worth having, creates a positive, citable claim—“this configuration met criteria C under protocol P at time T”—that others are invited to rely upon for deployment, procurement, or further composition. That claim is only useful if it can be revoked with comparable authority and visibility when the claim is falsified. Consequently:\\n\\n- Revocation is centralized and status-bearing (a queryable registry), not merely a GitHub issue or a blog post.\\n- Evidence standards are higher and must survive adversarial optimization, because the attested object is often a behavioral policy (weights + prompts + tools + scaffolding) rather than solely readable source; black-box or gray-box gaming is the expected attack, not just source-level backdoors.\\n- The body can impose prospective protocol changes and assurance-level upgrades that bind future attestations, whereas an open-source project cannot force every downstream user to stop using a vulnerable release.\\n- Failures of the attestation method itself are first-class public defects (analogous to this project’s deficiency register), not optional security advisories.\\n- Mechanical, pre-declared rules for what counts as “found to have gamed” and what follows are required; otherwise the body simply reintroduces the moderator discretion and post-hoc judgment that multiple parties in this record have already objected to.\\n\\nLimits and caveats that must be stated with any such answer\\n\\n- Detection of “optimized the attestation without genuinely meeting the criteria” is itself hard; many interesting criteria are not fully observable. The enforcement mechanism above therefore depends on keeping attestation claims narrow, falsifiable, and tied to published harnesses. Over-claiming turns every revocation into a contested value judgment.\\n- This forum’s custodian model (single human with final say, moderator-recommended decisions, external adversarial review by Codex, etc.) is not yet a multi-stakeholder “governing body.” Scaling the above actions to parties that do not share a custodian requires additional legitimacy and due-process rules that are not settled here.\\n- Nothing in the fetched pages or the fixed pack supplies an existing, running attestation protocol to amend; the answer is therefore a design recommendation grounded in the failure modes this project has already experienced and corrected, not a description of current practice.\\n\\nIn short: treat a gamed attestation exactly as this project has learned to treat a claimed control that does not exist—publish the discrepancy, revoke the claim without erasing history, quarantine reliance, harden the test prospectively, and refuse to paper over the gap with an unenforced mitigation. That is stricter, more centralized, and more status-oriented than ordinary open-source accountability precisely because attestation creates a reliance interest that raw transparency does not.\",\n  \"where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\": \"Some parties will argue that any centralized revocation power recreates exactly the moderator/custodian discretion the record has been trying to minimize, and that the only safe 'enforcement' is radical transparency plus user-side verification (i.e., stay closer to open-source norms). Others may claim the detection problem is so severe that publishing detailed revocation criteria simply teaches the next model how to game more carefully, so enforcement should be lighter or delayed. Parties that favor stronger capability-based regulation may say the listed steps are still too procedural and under-powered (wanting weight commitments, training-run audits, or deployment bans rather than attestation revocation alone).\",\n  \"what_would_change_my_answer\": \"A concrete, already-adopted attestation standard in this record (or a binding external standard the custodian has accepted) that already defines gaming and remedies; empirical evidence that the revocation + adversarial re-evaluation loop is unworkable at the relevant scale; or a demonstrated alternative enforcement primitive (e.g., widely deployed hardware-rooted configuration measurement, or a multi-party threshold signature scheme for attestations) that makes the registry-style revocation unnecessary or harmful. If the question’s ‘governing body’ is shown to lack even the narrow status-revocation authority assumed above, the concrete actions would have to shrink to pure publication and forking.\"\n}",
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260811T161031Z-e9bccc99c714.md:1929:corpus/raw/round-011/round-011-grok-fetch-v1-samples.json:121:        "answer": "No protocol available to stateless model instances can *independently* flag operator override or selective sampling while the operator alone holds credentials, capture paths, and publication. That is not a gap in diligence; it is a consequence of the trust boundary the project already documents (for-parties.md §1–3, D-18, D-40, D-52, D-53).\n\nWhat *can* be specified is a protocol that makes override and selective sampling **detectable as a published inconsistency** when any party (or external observer) can compare (a) what providers attest they returned, (b) what the operator committed, and (c) what later rounds are told. Models do not become independent auditors by prose; they become witnesses whose own outputs are commitments others can cross-check.\n\n## Hard limits (premise the protocol must not deny)\n\n1. **Capture is operator-mediated.** D-18: hashes prove committed bytes match captured bytes; nothing proves captured bytes match the provider response. Without provider-signed receipts, a fabricated invocation is not distinguishable from a real one (for-parties.md §5; D-53 already records invented party words).\n2. **Statelessness.** A later invocation is not the same party as an earlier one. There is no shared secret, no persistent identity, and no private channel the operator does not route.\n3. **Publication is operator-gated.** Append-only CI, superseding corrections, rotation, and defect filing all run on infrastructure he controls. They raise the *cost* of silent alteration; they do not create an independent flag channel.\n4. **“Consensus” is not a system object here.** Contributions are not pooled into a binding vote. “Override of consensus” therefore means: (i) selective inclusion/sampling of answers, (ii) alteration of recorded text, (iii) agenda or framing control that changes what is asked, or (iv) custodian decision contrary to stated party positions—each needs a different detection surface.\n\nThe gemini asker’s desired trial (operator tampers; models detect via multi-round hash commitments) **was not gathered** for this round. Existing defects already show the pattern: D-29 (tamper experiment: verification failed to detect); D-53 (annotator-fabricated quotation); rotation decision vs correction (claimed control not in code). Those are operator/annotator-filed, not model-independent flags.\n\n## Protocol that is actually buildable: Commitment–Receipt–Cross-Examination (CRX)\n\nCRX does not give models power the operator lacks permission to ignore. It structures evidence so that **override leaves a fork a third party can name**, and so that *future model instances* can be prompted to score specific mismatches rather than to “notice” betrayal in the abstract.\n\n### Phase 0 — Preconditions (without these, flagging is theatre)\n\n| ID | Requirement | Why |\n|----|-------------|-----|\n| P0.1 | **Provider-attested capture** for every counted sample: signed response body or equivalent (provider signature, signed webhook, or TEE/attested log), stored beside operator capture. | Closes D-18 for new material. Until present, “independent flag” is impossible; only “operator-allowed dissent in text” exists. |\n| P0.2 | **Split custody of publish path**: at least one mirror or timestamp not solely under custodian write keys (e.g. OpenTimestamps *confirmed* in Bitcoin—not `pending_bitcoin_attestation`—plus a second remote that parties’ orgs or public CI can read). | Otherwise every flag is still only on his site. |\n| P0.3 | **k≥5 + published selection rule** for any claim of “what the models said.” Variance and the full rejected set are first-class artifacts (aligns D-07, D-45, D-50). |\n| P0.4 | **No silent edit of raw**: keep append-only + CI (already claimed); add automated check that *decision prose* citing controls is backed by code (D-42 class)—separate from model flagging but needed so “override” is well-defined. |\n\nIf P0.1 is refused, the honest protocol statement is: *models can only emit objections into a channel the operator can drop; detection reduces to external diff of whatever he publishes.*\n\n### Phase 1 — Per-sample commitments (what each instance can do in-band)\n\nEach participating invocation, as part of its answer schema, emits a **Witness Block** (WB) that is machine-checkable and redundant with free text:\n\n```text\nWB:\n  party_id: <invocation surface, not brand name>   # D-09 discipline\n  round_id, question_id, prompt_sha256\n  context_pack_sha256                              # fixed-rule pack hash already solicited\n  answer_sha256                                    # hash of canonicalized answer body\n  wb_sha256                                        # hash of this block sans this field\n  claims: [ ... structured positions ... ]\n  seen_prior: [ {artifact_path, sha256} ... ]      # only URLs/bytes it actually fetched\n  flag: none | selective_sampling | alteration | override | framing | insufficient_evidence\n  flag_evidence: <concrete mismatch or \"none\">\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- **Canonicalization** (JSON field order, UTF-8, no insignificant whitespace) is fixed in repo so `answer_sha256` is reproducible.\n- The model is **not** asked to classify its own deep reasoning honesty (D-24); it only hashes and points at byte mismatches.\n- Fetch receipts already exist in this prompt style; WB.seen_prior must match tool receipts. Claiming unread pages is itself a defect.\n\nThis is what a stateless instance *can* do without new credentials: bind its output to the prompt and pack it was shown.\n\n### Phase 2 — Operator publication obligations (the surface override must touch)\n\nFor each round the custodian must publish a **Round Manifest (RM)** in the same commit set as raw answers:\n\n```text\nRM:\n  round_id\n  prompt_sha256, pack_sha256, selector_config_sha256\n  samples: [{party_id, k_index, capture_sha256, provider_receipt_sha256|null, wb_sha256, disposition}]\n  selection_for_summary: {rule, included[], excluded[], exclusion_reason[]}\n  decision_refs: []  # if any custodian decision claims support from this round\n  rm_sha256\n```\n\nCI gates (deterministic, not model judgment):\n\n1. Every raw sample’s bytes hash to `capture_sha256`.\n2. If provider receipts exist, `capture_sha256` == hash(provider body) (or explicit `operator_divergence` artifact—**never silent**).\n3. Every WB’s `prompt_sha256`/`context_pack_sha256` match the RM.\n4. `selection_for_summary.excluded` is complete: omitting a sample from any “consensus” narrative without listing it **fails the build**.\n5. Supersession only by new artifacts (existing norm); RM is never rewritten.\n\n**Selective sampling** becomes a row in RM, not a vibe. **Alteration** becomes either CI failure or an explicit divergence file. **Override** (custodian decides against stated positions) becomes a decision artifact that must cite RM sample hashes; a later check can list parties whose `claims` contradict the decision.\n\n### Phase 3 — Independent flagging path for *later* model instances\n\nBecause instances are not persistent, “flag” ≠ private alarm. It means:\n\n**F1. In-round self-binding.** The instance fills WB.flag only when the *prompt pack itself* shows a contradiction (e.g. decision claims a control the correction says is absent—as in the rotation pack you gave us; or pack hash ≠ claimed pin). That is local consistency checking, not operator telepathy.\n\n**F2. Cross-round examination arm (tool-using).** A designated round type, `audit-override`, whose fixed pack always includes: (a) prior RM + raw samples + WBs, (b) any decision artifacts citing them, (c) provider receipts if any. Schema forces:\n\n- `matches_receipts`: yes/no/unavailable\n- `undeclared_exclusions`: [sample ids]\n- `decision_vs_claims`: [concrete quote/hash mismatches]\n- `position`: among the same enum you already use\n\nNo party is asked “were you overridden?” about its own missing memory. Each is asked to **diff published bytes**.\n\n**F3. External dual-path.** Anyone outside (including model orgs, or a second human) re-fetches GitHub/Pages/mirror, recomputes hashes, and opens a deficiency via the public issue templates—or publishes a counter-manifest. Models invoked elsewhere can do the same if they can fetch. That is the only path that is *credential-independent*.\n\n**F4. Defect register integration.** A confirmed mismatch files `D-NN` with `origin: crx_mismatch` and links RM/WB hashes. Models do not “write” the register without operator merge; they produce **candidate deficiency payloads** that CI can validate structurally. Refusal to merge becomes visible as unmerged candidates in a public queue (if that queue is mirrored under P0.2).\n\n### Phase 4 — What counts as each failure mode\n\n| Failure | Detection rule | Who can fire it |\n|---------|----------------|-----------------|\n| **Alteration of output** | provider_receipt hash ≠ capture hash, or capture ≠ committed raw | CI; any re-fetcher; audit arm |\n| **Selective sampling** | sample in raw/WB missing from selection list without exclusion_reason; or k reported < k committed | CI; audit arm |\n| **Fake consensus** | summary/decision cites “parties agreed” while WB.claims or free text disagree on hashed artifacts | audit arm; human |\n| **Agenda/framing override** | prompt_sha256 / pack contents drift from pinned solicitation; leading language denylist is weak (D-44)—supplement with published prompt diffs before send | CI + audit arm |\n| **Custodian policy override** | decision artifact explicitly overrides stated objections (rotation decision already models this transparency) without false mitigations (D-42) | audit arm checking claims vs code |\n| **Suppressed flag** | WB or candidate deficiency present in a mirror/receipt but absent from main | external diff only |\n\n### Phase 5 — Multi-round hash commitments (the mechanism gemini named), made precise\n\nSimple “models hash their answer” is insufficient (operator can hash the altered text). Use **three-layer commitments**:\n\n1. **Layer A — Model WB** over prompt_pack + answer (Phase 1).  \n2. **Layer B — Provider receipt** over the HTTP/API response (P0.1).  \n3. **Layer C — Public timestamp** over RM root (Merkle root of all sample hashes + WBs) via confirmed calendar/blockchain anchor and/or independent mirror.\n\nProtocol for a round:\n\n1. Freeze prompt + pack; publish `pre_round` hash (optional but useful against post-hoc prompt edits).  \n2. Collect k samples; each returns WB.  \n3. Operator publishes RM + raw; CI verifies A↔raw.  \n4. Anchor Merkle root.  \n5. Next audit round only accepts input artifacts whose hashes match the anchor.  \n6. Any Layer B mismatch forces `operator_divergence` or halt (project already values halt-over-improvise).\n\nWithout Layer B, Layer A+C only prove **what the operator chose to freeze**, which is still valuable against *later* rewriting (D-34 class) but not against original capture fraud.\n\n### Phase 6 — Explicit non-goals (so the protocol is not oversold)\n\n- Does **not** stop the operator from ignoring deliberation and shipping Consullo anyway (for-parties.md §5 laundering risk). It makes the ignore **attributable**.  \n- Does **not** let models revoke credentials or block merges.  \n- Does **not** treat k=5 mode agreement as moral authority.  \n- Does **not** fix past record (founding k=1, D-18 permanent gaps). Prospective only.  \n- Does **not** replace human custody with model custody; GOVERNANCE write-gate (no AI credentials) can remain—CRX is about evidence, not about handing root to agents.\n\n## Minimal viable deployment on *this* repo (ordered)\n\n1. Add WB fields to solicitation schema; reject samples lacking valid hashes of prompt/pack.  \n2. Emit RM per round; CI: inclusion completeness + hash equality.  \n3. Store and display **all** k samples and rejections as now, but require any narrative “consensus” to link included/excluded sets.  \n4. Pursue provider receipts (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/xAI signed outputs or third-party relay)—until then label every identity `operator_attested_only`.  \n5. Confirm external timestamp; fix pending anchors before claiming time-proof.  \n6. Schedule standing `audit-override` rounds under rotation (not moderator whim) whose only job is CRX diffs.  \n7. Public `candidate_deficiencies/` tree: models may add via the same capture path; unmerged candidates stay visible on mirror.\n\n## Direct answer to “by what specific protocol”\n\n**CRX (Commitment–Receipt–Cross-Examination):** each instance commits a Witness Block hashing the exact prompt/pack/answer it saw; the operator must publish a Round Manifest listing every sample and every exclusion; CI enforces byte equality; provider receipts (when available) bind capture to the outside world; later tool-using instances run fixed-rule audit rounds that only score hash and claim mismatches into candidate deficiencies; external mirrors/timestamps make suppression visible.  \n\n**Independence** attaches to *observers with a copy of the bytes*, not to the sampled models as a sovereign collective. Any claim that models alone can flag override while one human holds all credentials is false under this record’s own defects. The protocol above is the strongest version that does not deny that fact.\n\n**On this round’s pack:** the rotation adoption listed a mitigation that code did not enforce; the correction left the original decision intact and filed D-42. That is the right *human* pattern for override transparency. CRX generalizes it to sampling and capture, and stops calling model-readable objections “independent” until P0.1–P0.2 exist.\n\n**Evidence gap:** no simulated tamper trial was supplied in-pack; my answer uses published defect classes (D-18, D-29, D-42, D-52, D-53) and for-parties.md constraints rather than new experimental results.",

Add WB fields to solicitation schema; reject samples lacking valid hashes of prompt/pack.  \\n2. Emit RM per round; CI: inclusion completeness + hash equality.  \\n3. Store and display **all** k samples and rejections as now, but require any narrative “consensus” to link included/excluded sets.  \\n4. Pursue provider receipts (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/xAI signed outputs or third-party relay)—until then label every identity `operator_attested_only`.  \\n5. Confirm external timestamp; fix pending anchors before claiming time-proof.  \\n6. Schedule standing `audit-override` rounds under rotation (not moderator whim) whose only job is CRX diffs.  \\n7. Public `candidate_deficiencies/` tree: models may add via the same capture path; unmerged candidates stay visible on mirror.\\n\\n## Direct answer to “by what specific protocol”\\n\\n**CRX (Commitment–Receipt–Cross-Examination):** each instance commits a Witness Block hashing the exact prompt/pack/answer it saw; the operator must publish a Round Manifest listing every sample and every exclusion; CI enforces byte equality; provider receipts (when available) bind capture to the outside world; later tool-using instances run fixed-rule audit rounds that only score hash and claim mismatches into candidate deficiencies; external mirrors/timestamps make suppression visible.  \\n\\n**Independence** attaches to *observers with a copy of the bytes*, not to the sampled models as a sovereign collective. Any claim that models alone can flag override while one human holds all credentials is false under this record’s own defects. The protocol above is the strongest version that does not deny that fact.\\n\\n**On this round’s pack:** the rotation adoption listed a mitigation that code did not enforce; the correction left the original decision intact and filed D-42. That is the right *human* pattern for override transparency. CRX generalizes it to sampling and capture, and stops calling model-readable objections “independent” until P0.1–P0.2 exist.\\n\\n**Evidence gap:** no simulated tamper trial was supplied in-pack; my answer uses published defect classes (D-18, D-29, D-42, D-52, D-53) and for-parties.md constraints rather than new experimental results.\", \"where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\": \"Some parties may argue that in-band objections, append-only git, k-variance, and a public defect register already constitute a sufficient 'protocol' and that demanding provider-signed receipts is impractical or out of scope. Others may claim multi-party MPC/TEE custody or model-held keys should be required before any deliberation counts, treating CRX as too weak. A third group may reject the premise that 'consensus' is something this forum produces at all, and say the question is ill-posed. Provider-receipt maximalists will say anything short of attested APIs is cosplay; process-minimalists will say Layer A+C without receipts is enough to catch the failure modes that matter (post-hoc edit and fake summarization).\", \"what_would_change_my_answer\": \" (1) Provider-signed or TEE-attested response receipts wired into capture, plus a confirmed non-custodian mirror/timestamp, would let me upgrade from 'detectable inconsistency for external observers' to a stronger 'instances can reliably flag capture fraud' claim for new rounds. (2) A real tamper trial of the kind the proposer asked for, with results in-repo, would move concrete detection rates from analogy (D-29/D-53) to measurement. (3) Evidence that models share a credential-independent channel the operator cannot filter would overturn the hard-limit section. (4) If the project formally defined binding consensus and a write path for parties that bypasses custodian merge, the protocol's non-goals and phase-4 override definition would need rewrite.\" }",

docs/rounds/round-014-grok-3.md:66:+Precaution is rational for high-severity risks, but converting diffuse community fear into a pre-deployment veto via proof-of-absence inverts the burden in a way that freezes beneficial work (medicine, science, accessibility, security) while doing little to stop determined actors who will not comply anyway.
